AMENDMENT_SEMANTICS.rule: APPEND-ONLY. The parent is left byte-unchanged. This amendment supersedes clauses ONLY in the single respect each SUPERSEDED_PARENT_CLAUSES entry states; every other word of the same clause continues to control.
AMENDMENT_SEMANTICS.how_to_read_the_two_together: Where this amendment is silent, the parent controls verbatim. Where this amendment names a parent clause under SUPERSEDED_PARENT_CLAUSES, that clause is superseded ONLY in the stated respect. A reader who has only the parent is reading a specification that was correct on B-1/B-2's premises and is now incomplete on two material points; a reader who has only this amendment is reading a delta and not a contract. Both are required.
what_this_amendment_does: (1) Registers MGP-PD2 - whether the hosted staging project's on_auth_user_created / handle_new_user trigger is active - as a new, unresolved measurement gap, and reclassifies PD-2 as CONDITIONAL on it (B-1).
(2) Re-derives PD-3 and PD-4 on bases independent of PD-2's conditionality, strengthening rather than weakening either.

(3) Corrects OD-P1's creation-channel options to remove a profile-write discriminator that does not survive B-1, preserving the genuine discriminators (operator credential, SSL-06, evidence strength, revocability, automation-fit).
(4) Records OD-P5's email=NULL incompatibility with the repository trigger.

(5) Corrects AUTH_RLS_MODEL's failure-semantics table to align with the CONTROLLING frozen facts F-M11-07, F-M11-15 and F-M11-16, separating REACHABLE-over-real-HTTP states from NAMED-BUT-UNREACHABLE ones, without reopening those facts (B-2).

(6) Records the proxy's own independent getUser() round trip and its cookie-mutation risk, corrects a false 'verbatim' label, corrects two citations, and records a GitHub-masking limitation, a revocation-locator design requirement, and a quiesce-specific INCONCLUSIVE reason code (NB-1 through NB-9).
(7) Corrects PRE-1's disposition from an occurrence question to a materialization question, per owner direction, and adds PRE-1B as the artifact that closes it.
It does NOT answer OD-P1 through OD-P6. It does NOT perform any hosted read. It does NOT create, promote or provision anything.

B1_TRIGGER_ANALYSIS.why_the_parent_specification_is_wrong_on: The parent's PD-2 ('It has NO row in public.users') was derived SOLELY from an application-plane grep of syncUserProfile's four call sites. That grep is silent on the DATABASE plane: a trigger firing on auth.users INSERT writes public.users from INSIDE the database, reached by EVERY creation channel (dashboard, Admin API, direct GoTrue signup all insert into auth.users), with no application code in the path at all. An application-layer discipline (never call the four syncUserProfile sites) cannot prevent a database-layer trigger from firing.
B1_TRIGGER_ANALYSIS.consequence: PD-2, PD-3, PD-4 and OD-P1 are corrected below. MGP-PD2 is registered as a new measurement gap.

PROXY_REFRESH_FOOTPRINT.measured: lib/supabase/proxy.ts:29-101 (updateSession), matched by proxy.ts:48-51 for /api/health/* like every non-excluded path, calls supabase.auth.getUser() at :76 - its OWN call, on its OWN createServerClient instance (lib/supabase/proxy.ts:47-70), independent of and PRIOR TO the handler's own call inside getVerifiedAuthIdentityResult() (lib/supabase/server.ts:22, lib/auth/identity.ts:113). updateSession() runs UNCONDITIONALLY for every matched path at proxy.ts:10, before the rate-limit block that is the only part of proxy.ts actually gated on the /api/ prefix (proxy.ts:12-15).
PROXY_REFRESH_FOOTPRINT.consequence: Each HTTP request the observation runner makes to EP-2 or EP-3 with a session cookie attached causes AT LEAST TWO getUser() round trips to the staging project's GoTrue - one in the proxy, one in the handler - not one. This does not contradict UNAVOIDABLE_WRITE_DISCLOSURE's ONE-sign-in bound (see QUALIFIED_CLAUSES_NOT_SUPERSEDED), which counts CREDENTIAL PRESENTATIONS, not round trips.
PROXY_REFRESH_FOOTPRINT.cookie_mutation_risk: @supabase/ssr's getUser(), when the access token is near or past expiry, transparently exchanges the refresh token and calls the cookies adapter's setAll - at the PROXY layer, lib/supabase/proxy.ts:55-66, which writes the refreshed cookie onto the response via NextResponse.next()'s cookies.set. An authenticated request to EP-2 or EP-3 can therefore carry a Set-Cookie header in its RESPONSE, produced by the proxy layer, wholly outside the observation principal's own session-minting step.
PROXY_REFRESH_FOOTPRINT.evidence_discipline: DELIVERY_CONTRACT.evidence_emission_allowlist.forbidden_fields already forbids 'any Set-Cookie or Cookie header' - no new prohibition is needed. This entry corrects the RUNNER'S OWN ASSUMPTION: evidence capture must not assume Set-Cookie appears only on an explicit sign-in call. It must be stripped from EVERY captured response in a run, including the ordinary EP-2/EP-3 observation responses.
PROXY_REFRESH_FOOTPRINT.why_this_does_not_change_minimum_privile: The proxy's getUser() call authenticates using the SAME cookie the runner already holds; it requires no additional privilege and mints no new session - it is the standard @supabase/ssr refresh mechanism every authenticated request in this application already undergoes. REQUIRED_OBSERVATION_CAPABILITY and MINIMUM_PRIVILEGES are unaffected. Only the write/round-trip COUNT implicit in UNAVOIDABLE_WRITE_DISCLOSURE is corrected.

CU-A-ADD-1.text: GitHub Actions automatically masks in logs only the LITERAL STRING VALUE of a value registered as a repository or environment secret (or explicitly passed to ::add-mask::). The access token GoTrue issues in EXCHANGE for the password, and the cookie value @supabase/ssr assembles from it, are DERIVED strings the platform has never seen as a registered secret and therefore CANNOT mask automatically. A workflow selecting CU-A MUST explicitly mask (via ::add-mask:: or equivalent) every derived token or cookie value BEFORE it can appear in any log line, and MUST NOT rely on the registered password secret's automatic masking to protect them.
CU-A-ADD-1.why_this_is_recorded_here: This is a control on the RUNNER'S OWN IMPLEMENTATION, not on the custody mechanism itself. CU-A's residual_risk analysis in the parent did not separate 'the registered secret is masked' from 'everything derived from it is masked' - they are not the same guarantee, and conflating them is exactly the kind of gap a masking assumption hides until a log leaks.

REVOCATION_LOCATOR_REQUIREMENT.problem: Revoking or rotating the principal - deleting the auth subject, or targeting a password/token reset - requires a way to LOCATE it, by subject UUID or by email, per the Admin API's or dashboard's own addressing.
REVOCATION_LOCATOR_REQUIREMENT.constraint_preserved: DELIVERY_CONTRACT.evidence_emission_allowlist forbids the subject UUID and the email address from ORDINARY per-run evidence (why_the_subject_uuid_is_forbidden_even_though_it_is_not_a_credential). That prohibition is NOT weakened by this requirement.
REVOCATION_LOCATOR_REQUIREMENT.design_requirement: Locating the principal for revocation requires a SEPARATE, RESTRICTED-ACCESS RECORD - held alongside the custody store selected at OD-P3, never inside the ordinary evidence stream - carrying the locator (UUID and/or email) bound to the principal LABEL (M11_OBSERVER). This record is NOT evidence and is not subject to EVIDENCE_CONTRACT's per-run rules; it is a CUSTODY-ADJACENT INVENTORY ARTIFACT, visible only to the named accountable holder CUSTODY_CONTRACT.custody_invariants_regardless_of_option already requires, and is covered by the SAME 'never in the repository working tree' rule as the credential itself.
REVOCATION_LOCATOR_REQUIREMENT.scope: Recorded as a DESIGN REQUIREMENT for LIFECYCLE phase 1 (CREATION, which must produce this record) and phase 5 (REVOCATION/EXPIRY, which must consume it). This artifact does not create the record; creating one remains a hosted-adjacent act no artifact in this lane authorizes.

QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON.extends: EVIDENCE_CONTRACT.per_run_evidence's existing INCONCLUSIVE reason codes (302 protection, 429 rate limit, transport error) with a fourth.
QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON.rule: If a governed QUIESCE or recovery posture has intentionally made GoTrue unreachable for the staging project at observation time, the run's sign-in attempt fails not because of a deployment fault but because of a DELIBERATE, GOVERNED posture change. This MUST be recorded INCONCLUSIVE with this specific reason code, NEVER FAIL - a FAIL would misattribute a governance decision to a deployment defect and would redden the M11 gate during a properly authorized maintenance window.
QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON.known_interaction: CG-Q4's G-2 names GoTrue as a writer that a QUIESCE empty-write window would exclude; UNAVOIDABLE_WRITE_DISCLOSURE.interaction_with_any_quiesce_or_read_only_posture already records that this principal's sign-in CONTRADICTS such a posture and that the observation must not run - this reason code is what the EVIDENCE looks like if a run is attempted anyway, or is attempted without the runner knowing a posture is active.
QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON.open_dependency: Detecting this reason code requires the runner to be able to ask whether a quiesce posture is CURRENTLY declared for the project - a capability this artifact does not specify. Until it exists, an operator reviewing a failed run must manually cross-check an active quiesce declaration before classifying a sign-in failure as this reason rather than as a genuine outage. This is carried forward alongside OF-P4, not resolved by it.
